newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crude outlook - MidEast crude outlook rosier.
newsitem.headline: Asia crude outlook - MidEast crude outlook rosier.

text.p: Asian produced crude found little sympathy from buyers last week and traders said they expected the pain to continue this week.

But signs late last week that MidEast crude was finding some support, pushing traded differentials back into premium territory, took a knock on Monday with news that India awarded just two Dubai cargoes; one to Total at first-half quotes plus 42 cents per barrel and one to Phibro at first half quotes plus 44 cents.
That left at least two cargoes exposed from a European major who was not awarded in the tender.
Traders attributed India's smaller appetite to the decision by the Indian Oil Corp (IOC) to take 3.6 million barrels of Iraqi crude under a term contract.

Indonesian benchmark crude Minas slumped to trade at ICP -50 cents per barrel after being talked a week earlier at ICP +20 to ICP +40 cents. Duri also slumped to ICP -50 cents, on the basis of deals talked in the market.
The price of both crudes were undermined by the 38-day maintenance of the 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) Dumai refinery, which started February 22.
Late last week traders estimated as much as one million barrels of Minas were still overhanging the market.
"I don't see any firming in the heavy sweet price until we hear of someone arbing out of the region," one trader said. "That would signal prices have bottomed."
Some traders said the price fall of heavy sweet grades had already been over done because some traders were panic selling.
"There are people who have to sell and are trying to get the crude off their books," one equity holder said.
But this trader added that outright prices needed to fall further to make Indonesian grades more competitive with MidEast and West African grades, which would add more pressure to the differentials.

MidEast grades, trading for April, mostly slumped last week to trade at a discount to their official selling prices (OSPs). Traders said MidEast governments had failed to adjust their January OSP low enough to keep the crudes attractive versus benchmark Dubai.
But if Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) is anything to go by, OSPs for February could prove better for the sellers.
ADNOC slashed February prices between $2.75 and $2.90 per barrel over the weekend, which would allow buyers to be more comfortable buying above OSP levels.
By late last week, a partial cargo of Murban was heard traded at ADNOC +1 cents, after earlier slumping to double-digit discount earlier in the week.
Oman also traded around flat, traders said on Monday after falling last week to a discount as low as 6.5 cents.
But the India tender award meant Dubai cargoes were available, adding to other MidEast grades that might not have been placed yet.
"Everyone will sit back and wait for the sellers to get more aggressive," one trader said.

The wider fall in crude futures was adding to the bearish view on the market, although in the short term the Brent and NYMEX could be heading for a period of consolidation after both falling sharply in recent weeks, traders said.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3081)
